html:
The Yuchi are a Native American people of the Southeast, now based in Oklahoma. Their language is an isolate, related to no other known tongue.

In the 1500s they lived in the eastern Tennessee River valley, near the Cherokee. By the late 1600s many had moved south into Alabama, Georgia and South Carolina, and settled near the Muscogee (Creek), whose confederacy they joined. Some went on to the Florida panhandle.

Epidemics and war in the 1700s cut their numbers. In the 1830s the remaining Yuchi were forced west to Indian Territory with the Muscogee, part of the removals known as the Trail of Tears. Most are enrolled today in the Muscogee Nation but keep their own identity, and a few still speak Yuchi.
sum: The Yuchi are a Native American people of the Southeast, now based in Oklahoma. Their language is an isolate, related to no other known tongue.
